title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: on the previous page (ending with point (1)), Grothendieck set up the arithmetic profinite Teichmüller extension 1 → π̂_{g,ν} → M_{g,ν} → N_{g,ν} → 1. Here M_{g,ν} is the π1 of the universal curve over Q and N_{g,ν} is the π1 of the moduli stack M_{g,ν} over Q. He mapped this extension into 1 → π̂ → Aut_loc(π̂) → Autext_loc(π̂) → 1, where 'loc' means preserving the inertia (cusp) classes. He conjectured that M'/T' ≅ Γ_Q always. This page (point (2)) moves from the standard base point to an arbitrary curve.

Step 1. Let k be any algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, not necessarily algebraic over Q. Let X be a curve of type (g,ν) over k and x ∈ X(k). Then:
- X is the fibre of the universal curve 𝒳_{g,ν,k} → M_{g,ν,k} at a geometric point ξ ∈ M_{g,ν}(k) = M_{g,ν,k}(k).
- x is a k-point of the universal curve lying over ξ.

Step 2. In (11) he names the fundamental groups:
- T_X = π1(M_{g,ν,k}, ξ), the geometric profinite Teichmüller group;
- the arithmetic group π1(M_{g,ν}, ξ) over Q;
- S_{X,x} = π1(𝒳_{g,ν,k}, x);
- its arithmetic analogue π1(𝒳_{g,ν}, x);
- π_{X,x} = π1(X, x).

Step 3. The fibrations X ⊂ 𝒳 → M give in (12) a commutative diagram of homotopy exact sequences, geometric over arithmetic:
- 1 → π_{X,x} → S_{X,x} → T_X → 1 (geometric);
- 1 → π_{X,x} → M_{X,x} → N_X → 1 (arithmetic);
- the cokernels of the vertical maps are both Γ_{Q̃/Q}, where Q̃ is the algebraic closure of Q in k.
The geometric groups do not depend on whether k is transcendental, by invariance of étale π1 under extension of algebraically closed fields in characteristic 0.

Step 4. (13): there is a canonical isomorphism M_{X,x} ≅ M_{g,ν}, defined up to inner automorphism. It comes from a path in the fundamental groupoid of the universal curve over Q from the standard base point x_0 to x. It induces an isomorphism of the exact sequences (12) and (5).

Step 5. Consequence (14): π_{X,x} ≅ π̂_{g,ν} canonically, modulo the action of M_{g,ν} (which contains Ŝ_{g,ν}). The ambiguity is not just geometric (Ŝ): it includes Galois, because there is no canonical identification of Q̃ ⊂ k with the Q̄ used for x_0.

Step 6. He names this an extra structure on the profinite outer group π_{X,x}, the 'arithmétisation canonique'. As continued on the next page, it is a reduction of the structure group of the Isomext_loc(π̂_{g,ν}, π_{X,x})-torsor:
- from the huge group Autext_loc(π̂_{g,ν})
- to the image N'_{g,ν} of the arithmetic modular group π1(M_{g,ν/Q}).
The next page refines this to a torsor P_{X,x} under M_{g,ν} (paths in the arithmetic fundamental groupoid) mapping to Isom_loc(π̂, π_{X,x}), in case N → N' is not injective.

Purpose: to give every hyperbolic curve over any algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 (e.g. a transcendental curve over C) a canonical 'arithmetic' structure on its profinite π1, coming from the Teichmüller tower over Q. This feeds into Grothendieck's discussion of an 'indiscernibility' principle.
errors: Notation slip in (11): the letters for π1 of the moduli stack over Q and π1 of the universal curve over Q appear swapped relative to (12) and the previous page. Consistent usage requires M_{X,x} = π1(𝒳_{g,ν}, x) (universal curve over Q) and N_X = π1(M_{g,ν}, ξ) (moduli over Q).
Subscript inconsistency T_x vs T_X; the subscripts on M_X / M_{X,x} also vary.
The line 'x ∈ Ob Pt(𝒳_{g,ν,k},k) ≃ Ob Pt(M_{g,ν,k}/k)' should read 𝒳_{g,ν,k}/k on the right; this appears to be a slip in the manuscript itself.

Implicit hypotheses: M_{g,ν} must be taken as the moduli stack ('multiplicité modulaire'), not the coarse space. Left-exactness of the profinite homotopy sequence relies on hyperbolicity (2g-2+ν > 0) and goodness / center-freeness of the profinite groups involved. Neither is stated, but both hold.

ideas.what: Homotopy exact sequences of the universal curve over the moduli stack, geometric over arithmetic, at a point of an arbitrary algebraically closed field k ⊃ Q
ideas.modern_name: Profinite Birman exact sequence / arithmetic outer Galois representation of the universal curve
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, 1984); Oda, Ihara, Nakamura, Matsumoto in the 1990s
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower with Γ_Q action), in outline only

ideas.what: Canonical isomorphism M_{X,x} ≅ M_{g,ν}, up to inner automorphism, via the arithmetic fundamental groupoid; hence π_{X,x} ≅ π̂_{g,ν} well-defined modulo the arithmetic modular group
ideas.modern_name: Change of base point in the arithmetic fundamental groupoid of the universal curve
ideas.where_published: SGA1 (groupoid formalism); the specific application is not published

ideas.what: 'Arithmétisation canonique': for a hyperbolic curve over any algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 (even one not defined over Q̄), a canonical reduction of the structure group of the Isomext_loc(π̂_{g,ν}, π1(X)) torsor from Out_loc(π̂_{g,ν}) to the image of π1(M_{g,ν/Q}). It is a canonical class of 'arithmetic' identifications of π1(X) with the standard surface group, independent of any embedding Q̄ → k.
ideas.modern_name: No standard name. Closest: Galois/GT-orbits of identifications of profinite surface groups; 'arithmetic structure' in combinatorial anabelian geometry (Hoshi–Mochizuki); GT-structures on profinite surface groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Not clearly credited. Related ideas appear in Nakamura, Hoshi–Mochizuki and Minamide–Nakamura (unsure of precise match)

missed.claim: A curve over an arbitrary algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, e.g. a transcendental Riemann surface, carries a canonical extra structure on its profinite fundamental group. This is a reduction of structure group to the image N' of the arithmetic modular group, i.e. an 'arithmetic' orbit of identifications with π̂_{g,ν} mixing mapping classes and Γ_Q. It is refined (next page) to a torsor under M_{g,ν} built from arithmetic paths.
missed.quote: C'est une structure supplémentaire sur le groupe profini extérieur π_{X,x}, appelée "arithmétisation canonique" : restriction du groupe structural
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This gives a conceptual, base-field-free formulation of how Γ_Q and the profinite mapping class group act on surface groups. It is close to the motivation for GT-structures and to the questions in combinatorial anabelian geometry about which identifications are 'arithmetic'. The named notion and its torsor refinement do not seem to appear as such in the literature.

missed.claim: The structure is intended to underpin an 'indiscernibility' principle (developed on the next page), comparing the information in the M_{g,ν}-torsor of arithmetic paths with that in its image in Isom_loc. This depends on the open question of whether N_{g,ν} → Autext_loc(π̂) is injective.
missed.quote: Mais si N_{g,ν} →épi N'_{g,ν} n'était un iso, il serait quand = plus fin de dire que via (13) ... on a un torseur canon
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Injectivity of the arithmetic modular group into outer automorphisms is a known theme: Belyi, Matsumoto and Hoshi–Mochizuki proved related injectivity results. The 'indiscernibility' framing was not developed further in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: Most of the page is routine homotopy-exact-sequence and base-point bookkeeping. The notable unpublished detail is the named concept 'arithmétisation canonique': a canonical arithmetic reduction of structure group on π1 of any curve over any algebraically closed field of characteristic 0. This is conceptually close to later GT / anabelian work but is not explicitly in the record.
transcription_corrections: The left margin note reads 'si Q̃ est la clôture alg. de Q dans k' and belongs to the third row of (12).
The third row of (12) reads roughly 'Γ_{Q̃/Q} ≃→ Γ_{Q̃/Q} → 1', with vertical arrows from M_{X,x} and N_X; the '→1' seems partly struck out.
In (14) the qualifier 'can.' sits under the inclusion: 'M_{g,ν} ⊃_{can} Ŝ_{g,ν}'.
'Ob Pt(M_{g,ν_k}/k)' is written with subscript h/k ambiguities; the field is k throughout.
